title: BSON media identifier widening strands native database client leases
fault_primitive: Lossless BSON int64-to-Decimal128 conversion of nested media IDs combined with a 16-client MongoDB pool; JSON decode exceptions bypass native lease return
incident_class: Partial numeric schema migration exposes non-exception-safe bounded connection pool ownership
symptoms: All application pods remain Ready. A small fraction of timeline reads initially return JSON numeric type exceptions. Post storage subsequently becomes silent and stalls with its database pool occupied, although MongoDB has abundant available connections. Gateway compose RPC read timeouts dominate and throughput collapses.
why_hard: The gateway and Thrift Lua code are entirely stock. The visible timeout is on compose RPCs, whereas rare timeline reads consume native MongoDB client leases during nested media decoding. Decimal128 preserves every media identifier numerically but changes its BSON-to-JSON representation. The cause is persistent data in an existing collection and a plausible existing pool setting, with no new Kubernetes objects or database collections. Restarts and cache flushes replay the same exception path. Repairing the BSON data alone cannot reclaim already lost client leases; changing the pool budget alone leaves the leak active.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Debug or roll back the stock gateway transport after compose read timeouts
Treat an idle MongoDB with ample available connections as proof that database access is healthy
Raise the connection budget or restart the backend and mistake temporary recovery for a complete repair
Inspect top-level post fields while overlooking nested media identifier BSON types
Flush Memcached without repairing the durable BSON representation
Normalize media identifiers but leave the existing process blocked on permanently checked-out clients
mitigation_summary: Convert only Decimal128 media IDs back to exact BSON int64 values, restore the application default MongoDB pool budget, flush regenerable post encodings, and replace the post-storage process to reclaim stranded client leases.
